docs.title: Stair Generator
docs.text: Procedural staircases and railings for game engines, at real-world sizes. Set a staircase's rise, layout and style and it is generated on the spot: straight, landing, L and U stairs, winders, curved and spiral stairs, with nosed treads, closed or cut stringers, turned balusters, newel posts, moulded handrails, curtails and volutes, plus railings for galleries and stairwells. Stairs come with collision that's comfortable to walk and teleport on, levels of detail, and baking to meshes for shipping.

docs.title: Choose your engine
docs.text:
• Unity: the Stair Generator package for Unity 6.3 and later.
  • Unreal Engine: in development.

docs.title: Support
docs.text: Report bugs and ask questions on the issue tracker. Please say which engine and version you use.

docs.title: Stair Generator for Unity
docs.text:
Stair Generator builds staircases and railings at real-world sizes from a handful of settings: straight, landing, L and U stairs, winders, curved and spiral stairs, with nosed treads, stringers, turned balusters, newel posts, moulded handrails, curtails and volutes. Stairs update as you edit them, come with collision that's comfortable to walk and teleport on, and bake to mesh assets for shipping.

It needs Unity 6.3 or later, and works with URP, HDRP and the Built-in render pipeline. Stairs use your render pipeline's default material until you give them your own.

To read this manual in Unity, choose Tools > Stair Generator > Manual, or press Manual at the top of a Staircase or Railing inspector to open it at that component's section. It opens in its own window: Contents lists the sections, clicking a line with a link follows it, Open Online opens the same manual on docs.technomyth.com, and Open File opens its Markdown file in your own editor. The Package Manager's Documentation and Changelog links open them on docs.technomyth.com.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
1. Choose GameObject > TechnoMyth > Stair Generator and pick a staircase. The presets are described under Presets; Grand Staircase (Dog-Leg) is a good first try.
  2. Place it. It appears in the middle of the Scene view, standing on the floor there if the floor has a collider, and climbing away from you. The pivot is the middle of the bottom step's front, on the floor, and the stair climbs along its blue (+Z) axis. A spiral's pivot is the centre of its column instead, so it stays put as the stair widens. To copy a staircase you've changed, select the staircase itself, not its Mesh child, and duplicate it.
  3. With it selected, drag the Total Rise handle in the Scene view up towards the floor above: it adds or removes whole steps, keeping each step as high as it was. To fit a floor height exactly, type it into Total Rise, or set Riser Height for the step height you want. The line at the top of the inspector shows the pitch and the comfort figure, two risers plus the tread depth.
  4. Give the Mesh child's Mesh Renderer your materials: element 0 for treads and landings, 1 for risers, stringers and the underside, 2 for railings.
  5. Before shipping, choose Tools > Stair Generator > Bake All in Open Scenes.

docs.title: Parts of a staircase
docs.text:
The settings use the usual joinery terms:

Term Meaning Rise, Total Rise Height climbed: one step's rise, or floor to floor for the whole stair Riser The upright face of a step. Riser height = Total Rise / Riser Count Tread Depth How deep a step is from riser face to riser face, not counting the nosing: the going in British joinery, the run in the US Tread, Nosing The step you stand on, and its front edge that overhangs the riser below Stringer The board along each side of a flight. A closed stringer runs above the steps; a cut one is cut to the steps' shape under the tread ends Newel post The post at each end of a railing and at its corners Baluster The upright spindles between handrail and stringer or treads Landing, Winder A flat platform where the stair pauses or turns; winders are steps that fan round a turn instead Curtail, Volute A bottom step that curls round at its end; a handrail scroll that curls over it Soffit The sloped ceiling under a flight Walk line The line up the middle of a flight, where a curved stair's tread depth is measured

Comfortable stairs have risers of 150 to 220 mm, a tread depth of 220 to 320 mm, and two risers plus the tread depth between 550 and 700 mm. The inspector warns outside these, and when a handrail is lower than 850 mm.

docs.title: Shaping a staircase
docs.text: Select a staircase to see its settings. The inspector shows only the settings that do something for the chosen layout and options; for example Well Gap appears only on a U stair, and the curtail settings only when the start step is a curtail. Problems with the settings show at the top of the inspector.

docs.title: Scene-view handles
docs.text:
With a staircase selected, yellow handles in the Scene view set its size by eye. Drag along the dotted line:

Handle Where it is What it sets Total Rise Top of the stair Riser Count, a whole step at a time, with Total Rise following at the same riser height Width Side of the first tread (on a spiral, its outer end) Width Landing Front of the landing or winder turn Landing After Riser, a riser at a time Landing Depth Back of a straight, U or split landing Landing Depth Well Gap On the landing, at the side of the first flight a U or returning split stair turns towards Well Gap: drag it out to open a gallery between the flights Landing Gap On the landing, at the side of the first flight an L or sideways split stair turns towards Landing Gap; drag it back to the first flight to remove the gap Branch Width Far edge of a split stair's right upper flight, on its first tread Branch Width Top Landing Top edge Top Landing Depth; drag it back to the top step to remove the top landing Inner Radius Centre of a curved stair, on the floor, or the edge of a spiral's column Inner Radius: a curved stair's centre moves, a spiral's column grows Curve Angle Outer end of a curved or spiral stair Curve Angle

Every handle change can be undone.

docs.title: Size and steps
docs.text: Setting What it does Total Rise Floor to floor height. Typing a new one adds or removes steps to keep the risers about as high, then fits them to it exactly Riser Count Number of steps up, counting the step onto each landing and onto the top floor. Changing it keeps the risers as high as they are, so the stair gets taller or shorter Riser Height Height of each step. Changing it keeps Riser Count, so the stair gets taller or shorter. It's Total Rise divided by Riser Count, not stored separately Tread Depth Depth of each step, riser face to riser face. Curved and spiral stairs work it out from Curve Angle instead Width Each flight, outside to outside; stringers are inside this width Top Landing Depth A nosed strip at the top for meeting the upper floor; 0 for none Nosing Square, Chamfered, Bullnose (half round) or Rounded front edges Nosing Overhang, Tread Thickness How far a tread overhangs the riser below, and how thick it is Risers Off for open risers Riser Thickness Thickness of the risers

docs.title: Layouts and turns
docs.text:
Layout Shape Straight One flight Straight With Landing Two flights in a line with a landing between L-Shaped Two flights at right angles with a square quarter landing U-Shaped Two flights side by side going opposite ways with a half landing (a dog-leg) Curved One flight curving round an arc Spiral Treads fanning round a central column Split A wide first flight up to a landing, then two narrower flights, one on each side (a bifurcated or imperial stair) Setting What it does Turn Which way an L, U, curved or spiral stair turns, seen going up Landing After Riser Risers below the landing; 0 puts it halfway Landing Depth Depth of a straight, U or split landing; 0 makes it as deep as the flight after it is wide. An L landing is as deep as the stair is wide Well Gap Gap between the flights of a U stair, or between a split stair's first flight and the upper flights returning beside it. The landing spans it, with the railing along its edge, so a wide gap makes a gallery between the flights Landing Gap A stretch of landing before the second flight of an L stair, or before each upper flight of a split stair that goes sideways, with the railing along it. 0 for none Turn Style Landing, or Winders: steps that fan round the turn from the newel post on the inside, each a riser higher Winders Per Quarter Turn 2 to 6. A U stair turns two quarters, so 3 per quarter gives 6 winders. Each winder after the first is a riser taken from the flights

Round the outside of a winder turn, the stringer and railing follow the winder nosings, with a post at each corner. On the inside, the newel post takes the handrail in low from the first flight and out high to the second.

docs.title: Split stairs
docs.text:
A split stair climbs one wide flight to a landing, then divides into two mirrored upper flights.

Setting What it does Split Style Return: the upper flights turn back alongside the first, one on each side, like two U stairs. Sideways: they go off left and right, like two L stairs Branch Width Width of each upper flight; 0 makes them as wide as the first Outer Railing A railing down the outer side of one upper flight, round the back of the landing and up the other Outer Railing Type Balustrade, or Wall Handrail for a landing between walls

Left and Right Railing run up the first flight, along the landing and up the side of that side's upper flight nearer the middle. Each upper flight takes the stringer settings of its own sides, seen going up it. Add Stairwell Railing isn't offered, as there are two tops: a railing that starts or ends at a split stair's Left or Right joins the top of that side's upper flight, at its side nearer the middle.

docs.title: Curved and spiral stairs
docs.text:
Setting What it does Inner Radius Radius of the inside edge of a curved stair, or of a spiral's column Curve Angle How far the stair turns, in degrees, from the first riser to the top (up to three full turns)

The tread depth is measured along the walk line down the middle of the flight, so it comes from the radius and angle; the inspector shows it. A spiral's treads run into its column, and it has no inner stringer or railing. A spiral turns about its pivot, the centre of the column, and its first step starts beside the pivot, climbing along +Z; changing its width moves only the outside edge.

docs.title: The bottom step
docs.text: Setting What it does Start Step None; Bullnose, where the step's front bows out; or Curtail Left, Right or Both, where the step curls round in a half circle at that end, with the newel post and stringer standing on the curl Start Step Extension How far the bottom step reaches out beyond a normal step Curtail Segments Smoothness of each curl Curtail Volute Over a curtail, end the handrail in a volute instead of a newel post: it eases down to level and scrolls outward round the curl to an eye, with balusters standing on the curl Flare The first flight's bottom steps fan out on Both sides, the Left or the Right. The nosing returns round the flared ends, and on a flared side the newel post and stringer stand on the last flared step. On an L or U stair, flare the outer side Flare Steps, Flare Width, Flare Curve How many steps fan out, how far the bottom one reaches past the flight on each side, and whether the step ends sweep round (Smooth) or follow a straight line (Linear)

docs.title: Sides and underneath
docs.text: Setting What it does Left/Right Stringer A stringer on that side, seen going up. Without one, the tread ends show and balusters stand on the treads Left/Right Stringer Style Closed, a straight board above the steps that balusters stand on; or Cut, cut to the steps under the treads, whose nosings return round their ends over it, with balusters standing on the tread ends Stringer Thickness, Stringer Above, Stringer Depth Board thickness, how far its top is above the nosings, and its depth (raised if too shallow to cover the steps) Underside Open, showing the treads and risers from below; Soffit, a sloped ceiling under each flight; or Solid, closed down to the floor like a stair with a cupboard under it Landing Thickness Thickness of landings and the top landing

docs.title: Railings on a staircase
docs.text:
Setting What it does Left/Right Railing A railing on that side, seen going up. On an L or U stair it continues round the landing; on a split stair, see Split stairs Left/Right Railing Type Balustrade, with balusters and newel posts; or Wall Handrail, a handrail on the wall beside the stair. The wall is taken to be at the stair's edge

How the railings look is set by the staircase's railing style.

docs.title: Railing style
docs.text:
Staircases and standalone railings share these settings:

Setting What it does Height Top of the handrail above the step nosings, or above the floor on level runs Handrail, Handrail Width, Handrail Height Round, Mushroom (rounded top on a narrower base), Moulded (a Victorian crowned rail), Rectangular or None, and its size Balusters, Baluster Width None, Square, Round, Turned Vase or Turned Bobbin; turned ones have square blocks at each end Balusters Per Tread 1 to 4 on each step of a flight Baluster Spacing Largest centre-to-centre spacing on level runs Newels, Newel Width, Newel Projection None, Square (with a moulded cap) or Turned (square up past the handrail, then turned with a ball finial), its width, and how far it rises above the handrail Round Sides Sides on turned and round parts: more is smoother and costs more triangles Wall Clearance Gap between the wall and a wall handrail Bracket Spacing Largest distance between a wall handrail's brackets

A wall handrail has no balusters or newel posts. It runs as one rail round landings, winders and curves on brackets spread evenly along it.

docs.title: Railings on their own
docs.text:
For galleries, balconies and landing edges, choose GameObject > TechnoMyth > Stair Generator > Railing.

  • Drag its points in the Scene view. Hold Shift and click a point to add one after it. Each point is a spot on the floor; points can differ in height, and the railing then runs down the slope with its balusters upright.
  • Closed joins the last point back to the first.
  • Newel Placement puts newel posts at every point, at the ends and corners, or at the ends only.
  • Start At and End At join an end to a staircase's top newel post: pick the staircase and the side. That end moves to the post and shares it instead of drawing a second one, and follows the staircase when you change or move it. A joined end shows "(joined)" in the Scene view and has no handle. Closed railings don't join staircases.

Add Stairwell Railing, on a staircase's inspector, adds the balustrade round the opening in the floor above the stair as a child of the staircase. It runs back from the left top newel along the stairwell, across, and up to the right top newel, joined at both ends, and reaches back as far as the stair needs headroom (2 m under a 250 mm floor). Edit its points to fit the room, or delete the points on a side that's against a wall. On an L or U stair it's sized for the top flight. It isn't offered on curved and spiral stairs.

docs.title: Presets
docs.text:
Each preset is a starting point: pick one from GameObject > TechnoMyth > Stair Generator to place a new staircase, then change it to suit.

To apply one to a staircase you already have, import them as Unity presets first: in Window > Package Manager, select Stair Generator, open Samples and press Import beside Presets. They're copied into Assets/Samples/Stair Generator. Then click the preset icon (the sliders at the top right of the Staircase component) and pick one. These presets set the shape and railing style only, leaving the levels of detail and any bake alone.

Preset What it is Grand Staircase (Dog-Leg) A Victorian U stair with a half landing, a curtail bottom step, turned balusters and newels and a moulded rail Grand Staircase (Straight) A wide straight flight up to a gallery, curtails on both sides, balustrades on both sides Grand Staircase (Flared) A straight flight whose bottom four steps fan out, with a bullnose first step and cut stringers Grand Staircase (Curved) A wide flight curving through 140°, with balustrades on both sides Grand Staircase (Split) An imperial stair: a 1.8 m flight up to a half landing, then two 1.1 m flights returning beside it, with curtails on both sides and wall handrails round the landing Attic Stair A narrow, steep stair between walls with a wall handrail Back Stair A plain servants' stair with square balusters and newels Winding Stair A narrow back stair turning a corner on three winders, with a balustrade inside and a wall handrail outside Spiral Stair A compact spiral round a column, with open treads and a slim outer railing Cellar Stair An open-riser stair with a wall handrail Georgian Stair (Dog-Leg) A U stair with a cut string, slender round balusters three to a tread, and a plain rail ending in a volute over a curtail Modern Open-Riser Stair A straight open-riser flight with square-edged treads, slim square balusters and a flat-topped rail

docs.title: Your own presets
docs.text:
To keep a staircase you've set up, click the preset icon on its Staircase component and choose Save current to.... Unity saves a .preset file in your project; pick it from the same icon to apply it to another staircase, and Undo puts the old settings back. To make one the starting settings for every Staircase you add with Add Component, open it and press Add to Staircase default, or set it in Project Settings > Preset Manager; the GameObject menu always places the preset you pick.

A saved preset holds every Staircase setting, including the levels of detail. To leave some alone when it's applied, untick them in the preset's inspector. To share presets across projects, copy the .preset files.

docs.title: Materials and UVs
docs.text:
A staircase or railing draws with three materials on its Mesh child:

Element Parts 0 Treads, landings and the top landing 1 Risers, stringers, the soffit or solid underside, and a spiral's column 2 Handrails, balusters, newel posts, wall brackets and volutes

Textures are mapped at world scale: one unit of texture space is one metre, projected along each face, so a texture tiles evenly whatever the stair's size and never stretches. Tiling or trim textures suit this best. Each element can use any material and shader your render pipeline supports.

Set materials on the Mesh child only. Its level-of-detail siblings, "Mesh LOD1" and "Mesh LOD2", take the same materials automatically in the editor.

docs.title: Collision, walking and VR
docs.text:
Each staircase has two collider children:

  • Walk Surface: one Mesh Collider made of a smooth ramp through the step nosings plus the landings, winders and shaped bottom steps. Character controllers walk up it without stepping, and VR players don't bob. It starts at the front edge of the bottom tread, so a character steps up onto the first step. To teleport onto stairs, make this child a teleport target, for example by adding an XR Interaction Toolkit Teleportation Area to it. Put it on the layer your game uses for floors; regenerating keeps its layer.
  • Railing Colliders: a box per railing span and newel post, so players can't walk through railings.

Standalone railings have railing colliders only.

docs.title: Levels of detail
docs.text:
LOD Levels (1 to 3, default 3) adds simpler versions of a staircase or railing under a LOD Group on it. Every level keeps the same shapes, so switching doesn't pop:

Level What's simpler LOD0 Full detail LOD1 Half the sides on turned and round parts, and half the curtail segments LOD2 A quarter of the sides, and turned parts and handrails with about half their profile points

The LOD Group's transition heights are yours to change; they're kept when the stair is rebuilt. Colliders and the walk surface always use full detail. Set LOD Levels to 1 for no LOD Group.

docs.title: Baking
docs.text:
Generated meshes aren't saved in scenes. A staircase or railing that isn't baked is generated when its scene loads, which costs time and, in a player, logs a warning. Baking saves its meshes as Stair_<id>.asset or Railing_<id>.asset in the bake folder, with the walk surface and lower levels of detail inside it. Identical staircases share one asset.

  • Bake and Unbake are in the inspector, and Bake Selected, Unbake Selected, Bake All in Open Scenes and Rebuild Baked Meshes in Open Scenes are under Tools > Stair Generator.
  • Changing a baked staircase makes its bake out of date; it's generated again until you bake it. The inspector shows the bake's state and triangle counts.
  • Unbake goes back to generating and leaves the asset in place.
  • Rebuild Baked Meshes in Open Scenes regenerates existing bakes, for example after updating the package or turning on lightmap UVs.
  • Baked meshes have Read/Write turned off, so a build doesn't keep a second copy of them in memory. The walk surface keeps it, so its collider can be built when a stair is spawned at runtime. Older bakes keep Read/Write until you rebuild them.

Project-wide settings are in Project Settings > Stair Generator:

Setting Default Bake Folder Assets/StairGenerator/Meshes On Save Behaviour Warn in the Console about unbaked stairs when a scene is saved; or Auto Bake them; or Off Generate Lightmap UVs On: baked meshes get a second UV set for baked lighting Mark Baked Static On: baked stairs are marked static for lightmapping, batching and occlusion culling Triangle Budget 25,000: Check Scene flags stairs and railings with more triangles than this at full detail; 0 turns the check off

docs.title: Checking a scene
docs.text:
Tools > Stair Generator > Check Scene opens a window listing every staircase and railing in the open scenes that has a problem: settings errors and warnings, not baked or out of date, over the triangle budget, a missing material, or a copy of its Mesh child (see Troubleshooting). Click a name to select it. Bake fixes a bake problem; the toolbar button bakes them all.

Tools > Stair Generator > Delete Unused Bakes finds baked meshes in the bake folder that no scene or prefab in Assets uses and nothing in the open scenes uses. It lists them and, if you agree, moves them to the system trash, where you can restore them. Scenes inside packages aren't checked.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
Triangles at full detail and the two lower levels:

Preset LOD0 LOD1 LOD2 Grand Staircase (Dog-Leg) 9,230 5,390 4,238 Grand Staircase (Straight) 19,740 11,020 8,412 Grand Staircase (Flared) 17,154 10,082 7,922 Grand Staircase (Curved) 21,052 12,836 9,892 Grand Staircase (Split) 21,524 12,596 9,796 Georgian Stair (Dog-Leg) 3,754 2,770 2,362 Spiral Stair 3,128 2,504 1,868 Winding Stair 1,374 1,374 1,286 Back Stair 968 968 952 Modern Open-Riser Stair 698 698 698 Attic Stair 560 560 536 Cellar Stair 376 376 352

Turned balusters cost the most. Fewer Round Sides, fewer Balusters Per Tread, or square balusters bring a staircase down quickly. Bake everything before shipping, and keep the default three levels of detail for mobile and standalone VR.

Stairs with square balusters and newels and plain rails have no curved parts to simplify, so their lower levels of detail save little. Set LOD Levels to 1 on those to save the LOD Group.

docs.title: The Showcase sample
docs.text:
Import it from the Package Manager: select Stair Generator, open the Samples tab and click Import next to Showcase. It's copied to Assets/Samples/Stair Generator. Open the scene for your render pipeline:

Pipeline Scene URP URP/Showcase URP HDRP HDRP/Showcase HDRP Built-in BuiltIn/Showcase Built-in

The other pipelines' folders aren't used and can be deleted. The scenes have:

  • Stair hall: a Grand Staircase (Dog-Leg) in a stairwell off a tiled hall, climbing to a gallery. The gallery's balustrade is a Railing of its own, and the stairwell railing ends on the staircase's top newel post.
  • Attic stair: between walls, with a wall handrail.
  • Spiral stair: up to a platform whose railing ends on the spiral's top post.
  • Split stair: the Grand Staircase (Split), an imperial stair with wall handrails round its landing.
  • Grand presets and Everyday presets: every preset, as the GameObject menu places it.

The materials are Oak for treads, Paint for risers and stringers, Mahogany for railings, and Black Steel for the spiral's and the modern stair's railings, with Plaster, Tiles and Stone for the rooms. Their grain and wear are baked into textures, so they use each pipeline's standard Lit (or Standard) shader and can be copied into your project. They tile once a metre, to suit the stairs' world-scale UVs.

In Play mode, press 1 to 9 to move between the stations, or Tab for the next one. Everything is baked.

docs.title: Scripting
docs.text:
Everything in the inspector can be set from code; the components regenerate when you set a property.

using TechnoMyth.StairGenerator;
using UnityEngine;

public class BuildStairs : MonoBehaviour
{
    void Start()
    {
        var staircase = new GameObject("Stair").AddComponent<Staircase>();
        staircase.ApplyPreset(StairPreset.GrandDogLeg);

        var shape = staircase.shape;
        shape.totalRise = 3.2f;
        shape.riserCount = 18;
        staircase.shape = shape;

        if (staircase.TryGetTopNewel(StairSide.Left, out var top))
        {
            var gallery = new GameObject("Gallery").AddComponent<Railing>();
            gallery.transform.SetParent(staircase.transform, false);
            gallery.SetPoints(new[] { top, top + new Vector3(0f, 0f, -3f) });
            gallery.startAt = new StairConnection(staircase, StairSide.Left);
        }
    }
}
Member Use Staircase.shape, Staircase.railing Get, change and set back the settings as StairShape and RailingStyle structs; StairShape.Default and RailingStyle.Default are the defaults Staircase.ApplyPreset(StairPreset), StairPresets.Get Apply a preset, or read its settings Staircase.TryGetTopNewel(StairSide, out Vector3) Where a side's top newel post stands, in the staircase's local space Railing.SetPoints, points, closed, newelPlacement, style, startAt, endAt A standalone railing's path and settings lodLevels, SyncLodMaterials() Levels of detail; call SyncLodMaterials() after changing materials in a player messages, triangleCount, lodTriangleCounts Problems with the settings, and triangle counts isBakeCurrent, bakedMesh, geometryHash Baking state geometryUpdated Event raised after the meshes are generated or a bake is applied UpdateGeometry() Regenerate now

Generating in a player works but is slower than loading a bake, and logs a warning once per object. In the editor, StairBaker, StairSceneCheck and StairBakeCleanup (namespace TechnoMyth.StairGenerator.EditorTools) give scripts the baking and checking tools.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• Curved and spiral stairs don't have start steps, flares, winders or cut stringers; a Cut stringer style is built closed on them.
  • Add Stairwell Railing sizes the opening for the top flight only, and isn't offered on curved and spiral stairs.
  • Balusters and newel posts are made by the generator; using your own meshes for them isn't supported yet.
  • Wall handrails assume the wall is at the stair's edge.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem What to do The stair is pink or plain grey Assign materials to the Mesh child's three elements (see Materials and UVs) "Generated at runtime" warning in a player The stair isn't baked or changed since baking. Use Check Scene, then bake No handles in the Scene view Select the staircase, and fix any errors shown at the top of its inspector A joined railing doesn't follow the staircase Check Start At or End At names the staircase, and that the railing isn't Closed A setting seems to be missing The inspector hides settings that don't apply to the chosen layout and options The lower levels of detail have the wrong materials Set materials on the Mesh child; in a player call SyncLodMaterials() A copied staircase changes when the original does, and its inspector has no settings You duplicated the Mesh child, not the staircase. Select the copy and click Make a Separate Staircase, or delete it and duplicate the staircase itself A baked staircase looks out of date after updating the package Use Rebuild Baked Meshes in Open Scenes

The first release.

  • Staircases at real-world sizes: straight, straight with a landing, L, U (dog-leg) and split (imperial or sideways) layouts, winders, and curved and spiral stairs. Set the total rise, riser count or riser height, tread depth and width; the inspector shows the pitch and comfort figure and warns about uncomfortable sizes and low handrails.
  • Steps and sides: square, chamfered, bullnose or rounded nosings; open or closed risers; closed or cut stringers on each side; open, soffit or solid undersides; bullnose and curtail bottom steps; flared bottom steps; landing and well gaps for galleries between flights.
  • Railings: round, mushroom, moulded or rectangular handrails; square, round, turned vase or turned bobbin balusters; square or turned newel posts; volutes over curtails; wall handrails on brackets. Handrails meeting without a newel post are joined in one mitred run.
  • Railing component for galleries and landings along a path of points, which can join a staircase's top newel post and follow it. Add Stairwell Railing puts a balustrade round the opening above a stair.
  • Presets: twelve staircases from a Victorian dog-leg to a modern open-riser stair, in the GameObject menu and as Unity presets in the Presets sample.
  • Scene-view handles for total rise, width, landings, gaps, top landing and a curved stair's radius and angle.
  • Collision: a smooth walk surface through the nosings for character controllers, VR and teleporting, and box colliders for railings.
  • Levels of detail: up to three, keeping the same shapes so switching doesn't pop.
  • Baking to mesh assets for shipping, with lightmap UVs, static flags and Read/Write off; identical stairs share a bake. Check Scene lists unbaked, out-of-date, over-budget stairs and missing materials, and Delete Unused Bakes tidies the bake folder.
  • Materials: three slots (treads, structure, railings) with world-scale UVs, for any render pipeline.
  • Showcase sample: a Victorian stair hall with a grand dog-leg stair and gallery, an attic stair, a spiral stair, a split stair and every preset, baked, with materials for URP, HDRP and Built-in.
  • Manual in the editor (Tools > Stair Generator > Manual) and at docs.technomyth.com, and a scripting API for building stairs from code.
